comment: Scenes scripts/bench.mjs walks. Each becomes two page loads — one per
runtime — because requestAnimationFrame has a single cadence per document
and two panes animating together would report the page's fps rather than
either runtime's (bench/bench.ts explains it in full).
Counts are stepped because a single rig says nothing on a fast desktop
GPU: the first runs of this instrument pegged both sides at the display's
refresh rate in every scene but the 20-player one, which can show no
crossover at all. The page caps count at 64 (8 columns of 8, about 80 CSS
px per cell at a 1280-wide window); a denser grid would be measuring
thumbnails. A rig's stage scale is the scene's one-per-pane scale divided
by the column count, so a step raises the number of rigs rather than the
amount of each one that is cropped away.
The reference draws a grid scene (mesh / held / rigid) into ONE canvas
through one batched SceneRenderer — its home ground, and the shape a
spine-webgl application is written in — and `many` into one canvas and one
WebGL context per player, which is what meets the browser's ~16-context
cap. Each row's stats line says which.
`--corpus <dir>` points the script at a directory holding a file of this
shape plus the rigs it names, for real-world skeletons that never enter
this repository.

scenes.name: 1 meshed rig animating
scenes.why: the deform tier working every frame — the cost this approach was doubted on

scenes.name: 4 meshed rigs animating
scenes.why: the first step where the reference gets to batch several skeletons into one canvas

scenes.name: 16 meshed rigs animating
scenes.why: an all-mesh grid — spine-webgl's home ground, and where this package should expect to lose

scenes.name: 36 meshed rigs animating
scenes.why: between 16 and 64, so a crossover has somewhere to be seen rather than jumped over

scenes.name: 64 meshed rigs animating
scenes.why: the page's cap: the heaviest deform load either side is asked for here

scenes.name: 1 meshed rig animating (canvas2d)
scenes.why: the default backend, and the one real Safari struggles with

scenes.name: 16 meshed rigs animating (canvas2d)
scenes.why: the default backend under a grid — the per-triangle path's own scaling

scenes.name: 1 held pose
scenes.why: dirty-skip home ground: unchanged meshes reuse their raster, the reference redraws regardless

scenes.name: 16 held poses
scenes.why: dirty-skip multiplied by 16 against 16 skeletons the reference must redraw every frame

scenes.name: 64 held poses
scenes.why: the same at the cap, where a redraw-everything renderer pays the most

scenes.name: 1 rigid rig animating
scenes.why: region attachments only — pure and one CSS matrix per slot on this side

scenes.name: 16 rigid rigs animating
scenes.why: a grid of rigid rigs: element count and compositing against one batched draw

scenes.name: 64 rigid rigs animating
scenes.why: the cap, where this side is holding roughly four thousand elements

scenes.name: 8 small players
scenes.why: independent players, under the browser's WebGL context cap

scenes.name: 20 small players
scenes.why: past the ~16-context cap: the reference needs one context per player, this package shares one
